summary: The walkthroughs' faults, each replayed as X4 walked it, before and after (X4's walk scripts on a throwaway copy, Xvfb, X4's stand-ins, the Power Home through its own door; 1920x1200 and 1366x768). (1) A fetch is verified only when it is whole and the network is up as it is checked: its declared length and the connection's end are read, a fetch in flight is cut when the network reads offline, and a step whose page came cut short (or is checked while the network is down) is 'blocked: needs the network', never done; NET never says 'her fetch' while offline (network_governed, assignments). (2) Her own area's standing grant authorises a proposed step writing there (X4's C now runs); 'Grant this for this assignment' is offered and authorises its step while HALT holds, nothing runs, and after RESUME the held assignment's own Resume is a row in Waits for you that carries it through (grants, assignments, waits_qt). (3) TRACE (and the rest of her column's six) acts on the card focused on the board, and a card chosen by its own press skips the words-reading routes that asked 'Which of these did you mean?' (her_column_qt, shell2). (4) Her column reads her journal at once after a start (a quick gathering of its own; FINDINGS from their own gathering; 'Reading her journal…' / 'Reading the desk…' until then, never 'No assignment is open' while unread); a failed read is never kept as 'nothing'; her model line, ring and 'her model is answering' follow brain.status read with her work; ACTIVE WORK follows Stop at once (floor, her_column_qt). (5) HALT and RESUME make their Kernel part on a thread of their own; CHECK ALL is rehearsed on a thread with a recording Kernel and performed on the window's thread from its recorded reads; TRACE's line is read first on a thread; asking her no longer lays out the whole Field again, and 'look up …' asked in her column plans its step off the window's thread (off_window.py, halt, halt_qt, desk_doers, network_qt). (6) The HALT moment stands under Waits for you (overlap 31304 px before, 0 after). (7) Search matches every word on its own, finds Home's files and folders by name (a budgeted walk), lists each name once with the desk's object first, opens a hit on the board's focus (never the Cabinet record tab), and keeps the results in front, Back included (search_reach.py, console_qt, living_nav_qt). (8) Every keyboard stop gets a name a screen reader can say when it takes the focus, a scroll area holding presses hands Tab on to them, and the writing line no longer keeps Tab when there is nothing to complete (a11y_names.py, shell2).
decisions: Item 1, strict: any page checked while the network reads other than online is 'blocked: needs the network' (the coordinator's 'check the network's state at verify time'), even one that came whole; a page cut short with the network up (or past Graphite's own 2 MB) is 'needs review: cut short', never done. What came is kept in quarantine marked cut short with why. A fetch in flight is cut when a fresh reading says offline (not when the state is merely not known).

Item 2: K3 had the built-in 'her own area' grant never authorise a step by itself; F3's brief overrules it: it now authorises a proposed step writing there, through the same _grantable rule (never the model's pick alone, never what always asks or is marked for approval).

Item 2: K3 offered no grant press while HALT holds; F3 offers it (the plan speaks of a grant given while HALT holds). It authorises the step and says it runs when resumed; nothing starts until RESUME and the assignment's own Resume, now a 'Resume' row in Waits for you (HALT's own words already promised it there).
Item 3: the six presses in her column act on the card focused on the board when the board is in front (the Field's selection follows it: one selection).

Item 4: her column draws what each gathering brought (work, findings, cards) instead of waiting for one whole reading; at a start each gathering runs on a thread of its own, never behind the floor's queue.

Item 5: rather than rewriting each press, a press's reads are rehearsed off the window's thread with a Recorder (reads kept, changes refused) and the press then runs unchanged on the window's thread with a Replayer answering only those reads; every change still runs for real on the window's Kernel.

Item 7: Home is walked by name with a budget (80 ms, 20 000 names, 7 folders deep; hidden folders and Graphite's own workspace left out) and says when it stopped early; a cabinet record with the name of a desk object opens that object on the board.

Item 8: names are given at focus time from what a part shows (its words, its tooltip's first sentence, its placeholder), never from an internal object name; the links inside the console output stay reachable by Tab (a read-only text with links is not made to skip them).
findings_for_the_coordinator: The walks' harness distorts every off-thread timing: under its processEvents/QTest.qWait loop a 0.14 s Kernel read on a worker thread takes 7 to 11 s (GIL starvation); under the window's own app.exec() it takes 0.14 to 0.19 s (b100/F3/probe.py runs). So 'her column lags behind presses' and the seconds X4 saw for Waits for you after RESUME are partly the harness. Under app.exec on Rail Demo after F3 (probe3): TRACE answered in 0.24 s and 0.17 s, CHECK ALL 0.69 s, HALT 0.04 s, RESUME 0.05 s, the window's longest stall 125 ms (Qt or the system). Before: TRACE asked 'Which of these…' (stall 166 ms), CHECK ALL stalled 725 ms. A walk that measures latency should drive app.exec() with timers.

X4's assignment A ('Groceries note in ~/Documents/Notes') cannot finish before or after: its line's money total arrives in the step's output as a JSON number with a point, and K1 refuses to put it into words ('a value with a floating point is not put into words here'). The grant pressed while HALT holds does carry it to that point (authorised, run after RESUME and its own Resume). The line language's sums (in the seed) would need to give exact decimals as strings for a note to quote them; not changed here (the seed and K1's rule).

'startup duration' still finds nothing: in this tree no record or desk object holds both words in its name, kind, role, place or lines (X4 said both stand on one finding; not found). Search now matches each word on its own, so any object holding both is found.

Her column's whole desk reading (investigations, sheets and field.read on X4's 284-object desk) took about 4 s on a worker in the walk; FINDINGS now come from their own gathering first and say 'Reading the desk…' meanwhile.

Measured again on this tree before F3 (F2b merged): the board's rebuild after a cell change 0-164 ms (X4: 2118 ms), asking her 0-463 ms (X4: 1766 ms; the rest was desk_doers.in_sight laying out the whole Field again, now reusing the last placing), HALT 936-1075 ms and RESUME 458-690 ms (X4: 1.5-1.8 s), TRACE 815-1092 ms, CHECK ALL 2273-6640 ms (X4: 4.2 s).

The keyboard pass before F3 in a fresh window: 4 stops with no name of their own (a label, CentreFind, HerNoModelRoom, the centre's scroll area), the scroll area with none a reader can say; Storage's Mount and Eject safely were reached in this tree; but Tab never left the writing line while it held words in Search mode (it completed in place), a trap X4's pass did not meet because its line was empty.

My own harness had a fault worth knowing for any builder reusing X4's run.sh: its area is named by the shell's process number, which is 3 in every unshare'd namespace, so two runs at once share one area (one stall log, one Xvfb number). Fixed in F3's copy (mktemp); the before-1366 stall numbers (HALT 1075 ms, CHECK ALL 6640 ms) were taken while another run shared the area and may hold its stalls; the 1920 numbers were not.

At 1366x768 her column shows one row of ACTIVE WORK when something waits, so the Stop pressed on one assignment leaves the other in the row (by design, D1); the row's state word rests in its shape there.

Measured with the final code: under the window's own event loop (probe3, Rail Demo) TRACE 0.14/0.17 s, CHECK ALL 0.74 s, HALT 0.06 s, RESUME 0.04 s, asking her a lookup 0.05 s, every one with no stall over 100 ms. In the walk harness on X4's desk: HALT and RESUME 0 ms on the window's thread (936/690 ms before), the board after the cell change 0 ms, asking her 261-280 ms (1273-1436 ms before in session 8; what is left is shell2.ask's own start: relevance.note_request and its Kernel), 'Try it now' 328 ms (network_qt.retry on the window's thread), the first tree read 1.1-1.6 s (cabinet_qt, F2b's area, unchanged by F3).
not_done: Nothing tested in the owner's sense; nothing ran on the ThinkPad. No real network, NetworkManager, model or screen reader here: stand-ins only (X4's NetworkManager and web stand-ins; brain.status stood in for the model line; Qt's QAccessible names read in place of AT-SPI).
X4's assignment A still stops on its line's floating-point total (see findings); the grant-while-held path is shown complete on an assignment whose note quotes the sheet's cells.
The time an answer takes after TRACE or CHECK ALL in the walk harness is long (the harness starves worker threads); measured fast only under app.exec on Rail Demo, not on X4's 284-object desk.
Search's 'startup duration' (no object found holding both words); Search has no history of its own searches.

In the walk harness (processEvents/qWait), TRACE's and CHECK ALL's answers arrive after the walk stops waiting (20-25 s) on X4's 284-object desk: their reads run on worker threads that the harness starves. Under the window's own event loop (probe3, Rail Demo) they answer in 0.16 s and 0.65 s. Not measured under app.exec on the 284-object desk.

Still on the window's thread over 100 ms in the harness: shell2.ask's start (relevance.note_request, about 0.28 s on X4's desk), network_qt.retry ('Try it now', 0.33 s), the tree's first read at a start (1.1-1.6 s, cabinet_qt) and the Machine page's first build (machine_qt, 1.9 s before).
release_note: The walkthroughs' faults, fixed: a fetch cut short when the network drops is never 'done': the step reads 'blocked: needs the network', and the network word never says 'her fetch' while offline. A grant you give while HALT holds carries its assignment through once you press RESUME and its own Resume, which now waits for you in 'Waits for you'; her own area's standing grant covers her steps there. TRACE traces the card focused on the board. Her column says what her journal holds at once after a start, follows her model's state and your Stop. HALT, RESUME, TRACE and CHECK ALL no longer hold the window. The HALT notice never covers 'Waits for you'. Search matches every word, finds your home's files by name and opens a hit on the board, with the results kept in front. Every keyboard stop has a name a screen reader can say, and Tab no longer sticks in the writing line.
